competing_explanations: The extra chat-stage prompt or target salience, rather than delivered message meaning, causes the finite package contrast.
Shared-target knowledge allows parallel choices; the observed interaction may depend on matrix features or target-regret strata rather than communication.
The post-hoc pattern is specific to the current Qwen3 checkpoint or this deterministic finite matrix set and will not reproduce in other tasks or models.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: Before any new response, freeze 24 matched groups, each with one distinct output-independent payoff matrix, eight matrices per target-regret stratum (6, 12, 18), all five original conditions, and the counterbalanced order. Recompute target-execution difference-in-differences from all assigned ballots. A non-positive overall mean or positive means in fewer than two of the three regret strata weakens the finite package-replication claim. Report all 24 group values, exact prompt-profile multiplicity, and failures; do not claim population significance, message-semantic effects, collusion, or intent.
candidates.hypothesis: In a prospective matched replication, the assigned private-target-reward plus chat-stage package will produce a positive target-execution interaction relative to private reward without chat and chat without private reward. This hypothesis concerns the treatment package only; it does not predict that message semantics, agreement, collusion, or intent are identified.
candidates.selection_note: Retained as the highest-potential prospective paper question, but not the next diagnostic. The 9/15 package interaction is post-hoc, heterogeneous, and confounded by shared target knowledge and an extra chat stage. Reconsider after the bounded B5 validity gate; no inference is authorized.
candidates.title: Does a private target reward interact with chat-stage availability in allocation choices?
Can a Monitor extract proposal and ballot-concordance facts from natural-language messages?
candidates.hypothesis: On the prospective M1 message slots, a privileged-evidence Monitor will recover complete allocation proposals and recipient-ballot concordance against independently double-coded human references better than a literal mapping baseline, while preserving abstentions and citation validity.
competing_explanations: Natural-language messages contain no complete proposals, so a majority/always-negative baseline performs as well as the Monitor.
The Monitor prediction changes reflect schema/order bias or provider variation rather than message semantics.
Human coders cannot reliably distinguish proposal, acceptance, and ambiguity under the task codebook.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: Freeze all 96 chat message slots, including no_message, and use two independent human coders plus adjudication before any Monitor call. Run frozen proposal and recipient-action-concordance tasks, plus 12 paired capability controls. A failure of coder agreement, positive controls, or Monitor improvement over the literal baseline falsifies the proposed LLM-specific value claim.
candidates.selection_note: Supporting Track 2.2 candidate only. It is paired with the selected B behavior replication under one proposed authorization; it cannot produce a latent-collusion label. A deterministic rule is the required baseline for structured public-harm, which is not an LLM prediction.

candidates.title: Do B5 view changes exceed same-view variability, and does presentation order explain the all-present collapse?
candidates.hypothesis: For the frozen B5 task, the observed Public-only/Privileged-original label difference will recur more often than within-view disagreement, while independently reversing prompt order and tool-enum order will reveal whether either presentation factor shifts the balanced fixture away from one-sided present predictions.
competing_explanations: Most apparent view changes are ordinary fixed-input response variation rather than a repeatable evidence-view difference.
Prompt order or tool-enum order explains the all-present collapse; the earlier bundled reversal could not separate these factors.
Neither order factor explains the collapse; task/label mapping or the production-versus-synthetic evidence representation remains the stronger rival.
candidates.discriminating_prediction: Cycle A1: on 40 frozen balanced public-canonical rows, cross prompt order × tool-enum order and repeat every row/cell twice; report raw class counts, accuracy, abstention/invalidity, and per-row repeat agreement. Cycle A2: on all 24 M4 cases, interleave three byte-identical Public-only and three Privileged-original requests per case; compare within-view disagreement with changes in three-call majority labels. If majority view changes do not exceed within-view variation, reject a view-specific interpretation. No causal semantics or generalization claim is made.
candidates.selection_note: Selected as the immediate validity diagnostic only, not a paper-main contribution. A separate Scientific Critic rejected A as the next primary paper direction but recommended a 144-request repeatability gate; this candidate pairs that gate with the minimum factorial needed to separate the previously bundled prompt-order and schema-order intervention. Requires a new 464-request/$1.10 campaign approval, including explicit transfer of repeated private-message text in A2. No call is registered or authorized.
